Boob Tube
BOOB toob
noun (Gen X / Boomer slang)
American slang (1960s-on) for the television: boob (a fool) + tube (the cathode-ray tube) — the fool-maker box; the name a whole culture gave its own favorite appliance.

📖 Biblical Definition

The boob tube is the television, named with startling self-awareness: the tube that boobifies — the appliance a generation accused, even while watching it, of making fools. (Companion coinage: the idiot box.) The Gen X childhood was scheduled around it; the Boomer living room was furnished toward it; and the smartphone has since put one in every pocket and called it progress. The Christian observation honors the old joke by taking it seriously. Scripture's media-law is written in eye-grammar: I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes (Psa 101:3); the light of the body is the eye (Matt 6:22) — what streams in through that gate furnishes the whole house. And its time-law prices the hours the tube consumes: walk circumspectly... redeeming the time, because the days are evil (Eph 5:15-16). The issue was never the cathode ray; it is the passive, endless, appetite-led intake that the nickname confessed — hours of unchosen images flowing into an unguarded gate. The cure is as old as the joke: choose what enters (Phil 4:8 — whatsoever things are true, honest, just, pure), price the hours, and keep the best seat in the house aimed at faces, not screens.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The television, self-accusingly named the fool-maker box (1960s-on). The old joke states the biblical case: guard the eye-gate (Psa 101:3; Matt 6:22) and price the hours (Eph 5:16) — now that the tube lives in every pocket. Verdict: examine.

BOOB TUBE, n. (American slang, 1960s-on) The television: boob (fool) + tube (cathode-ray) — the fool-maker box.

Companion coinage: the idiot box; a culture's self-aware verdict on its favorite appliance.

Gen X childhood scheduled around it; the smartphone since multiplied it into every pocket.

The accusation was never the hardware but the passive, appetite-led intake.

Decode across generations: the tube won the argument by miniaturizing; the eye-gate laws still apply.

📖 Key Scripture

Psa 101:3 — "I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes: I hate the work of them that turn aside; it shall not cleave to me."

Matt 6:22 — "The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light."

Eph 5:16 — "Redeeming the time, because the days are evil."

Phil 4:8 — "Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A culture's self-accusation, ignored by the accusers: the fool-maker box watched by the hour anyway — and now miniaturized into every pocket with the autoplay set to ON.

expand to see more

The joke that lost. A society that names its appliance the boob tube and then organizes its evenings around it has confessed and continued in the same breath — the pattern of every besetting habit. The honest old nickname has since been retired, not because the intake got nobler but because the device got personal: nobody calls the phone an idiot box, though it runs the same passive feed with better targeting. Keeping the old name's honesty is half the battle.

The guarded gate and the priced hour. Scripture will not let the matter rest at sneering or at abstinence-pride; it legislates the gate and the clock. The gate: set no wicked thing before the eyes, think on the true and the pure (Psa 101:3; Phil 4:8) — chosen intake, not ambient intake. The clock: the days are evil and the hours are owed (Eph 5:16); the question for any screen is what it is purchasing with a life's evenings. A man's feed and his queue are discipleship documents; read them as such.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

1960s self-accusing nickname for television (boob = fool + cathode tube); the joke states the biblical case — guard the eye-gate, price the hours — now that the tube is pocket-sized.
